LESSON: TIME

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement 2.1 Length 10
Topic 2.6: Time

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Time. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Welcome to a mathematics program for grade four. Today, we shall learn about telling time in a m and p m. in this lesson we will require a pen or a pencil, a rubber and writing material. Welcome to Mathematics Lesson for grade four. Today, we shall learn how to tell time in a m and in p m. Learner, how many hours are there in a day? Good. 24 hours. Now, the 24 hours are divided into two equal cycles. Yes, 24 hours are divided in two equal cycles. The first cycle starts from midnight and ends at midday. This is referred to as morning. Yes, morning means from midnight to midday or noon. Learner, Midday is also known as noon. Learner, The time from midnight to Midday is in am cycle. The time from midnight to midday is in A M cycle. Learner, remember a day has 2 equal cycles, meaning that in the first cycle, there 12 hours. The second cycle begins from midday to midnight. The second cycle begins from midday or noon to midnight. The cycle from midday or noon to midnight is referred to as afternoon or evening. The cycle from midday or noon to midnight is referred to as afternoon or evening. Learner, the time from midday or noon to midnight is in p. m. cycle. The time from midday or noon to midnight is in p. m. cycle.

Learner, the following activity you do will help you understand further on how to tell time in either A M or P M. Listen attentively to the questions and write your answer in either A M or P M. A. What time do you go to bed? What time do you go to bed? B. What time do you wake up? What time do you wake up? C. What time do you go to school? What time do you go to school? D. What time do you go for lunch? What time do you go for lunch? Learner, if your answer are as below, then you are correct. Question A. You go to bed either at eight p. m. or 9: 00 p. m. or even 10: 00 p. m. For Question B. You wake up either at 5: 00 a. m. or 6. 00 am or even 7. 00 a. m. For question C you go to school at 5. 00 am or 6: 00 am or even 7: 00 a. m. And for question D. you go for lunch at 12. 30 pm. 12. 40 pm, or even 1. 00 pm. Give yourself a pat on the back for a job well done. Learner, one more thing to remember. Telling time in am or pm informs us of the activities we could be doing at that particular time, for example. 7. 30 am, you could be walking to school. But 7. 30 p. m., you could be having dinner at home with your parents or guardians.

In conclusion. Do the following exercise and share your answers with your parents, guardians or friends. In conclusion. Do the following exercise and share you answers with your parents, guardians or friends. Write the time in either A M or PM. in question 1 to 8. Question 1. Mary woke up at 6. 15 ______ to start off her day. Mary woke up at 6. 15 ______ to start off her day. Question 2. Aisha finished washing her clothes at 12. 40 _____ and then took her lunch. Aisha finished washing her clothes at 12. 40 _____ and then took her lunch. Question 3. Naliaka brought cows home at 5. 50 ______ and started preparing super. Naliaka brought cows home at 5. 50 _________ and started preparing super. Question 4. Ali took dinner at 8. 55 ________ in the evening. Ali took dinner at 8. 55 ______ in the evening. Question 5. The first lesson began at 8. 15 _______. The first lesson began at 8. 15 ________. Question 6. Three hours after midnight. Write the time in either a. m or p. m. I will repeat. Three hours after midnight. Write the time in either a. m. or p. m. Question 7. Two hours after midday. Two hours after midday. Question 8. One hour, fourty minutes after midnight. One hour, fourty minutes after midnight.

Learner, I will go over the 8 questions as I conclude our lesson today. Mary woke up at 6. 15 ______ to start off her day. Question 2. Aisha finished washing her clothes at 12. 40 _____ and then took her lunch. Question 3. Naliaka brought cows home at 5. 50 ______ and started preparing super. Question 4. One hour, fourty minutes after midnight. Good bye, learner. Be safe. Till we meet again. bye. your radio teacher was Scholah Mkandoh. SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Time means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Time.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER
